scope: Read-only review of final Swift file-conversion wrapper, raw-plane bridge, RIFF writer and focused test source/log. C arithmetic review referenced separately.

checks.area: RIFF byte counts and integer bounds
checks.result: Header is 56 bytes; RIFF size is payload+48, fmt tag is 3, fact count is frames, and data size is frames*channels*(precision/8). Preflight division bounds all UInt32 conversions, products and additions before header construction, including binary64. Integral positive sample-rate/byte-rate check prevents truncation and UInt32 multiplication overflow.

Source float64 selects planar float64 decoding; output preserves UInt64 sample bits directly rather than converting through Float. Other decoded sources use float32. Chunk buffers hold at most 8192 frames; final length and total file bytes are checked.

checks.area: Swift to C bridge lifetime and bounds
checks.result: Scratch is owned for the processor lifetime and freed once. Validated planar format/count/capacity and scoped nested buffer-pointer calls keep channel arrays, queues and points alive through the synchronous C call. File conversion uses private AVAudioPCMBuffer allocations with maximumFrames=8192. Tests exercise corresponding input/output aliasing through C staging.

Resolved path plus inode checks reject the source and hard/symbolic aliases. The same-directory temporary is removed on throw. Synchronize and close complete before move/replace; no destination update occurs for decode or processing failures. Existing-output replacement and late-block rejection are covered by retained tests.

All 12 channel/precision/direction combinations compare every output sample byte across the 8192-frame boundary. Separate Core Audio readback checks the final 17-frame tail and one-ULP sample, detecting binary64 narrowing. Tests additionally cover replacement, malformed input, aliases, late-block failure cleanup and preflight integer extremes.

retained_test_evidence.note: Inspected final test source and retained peer-run log; did not rerun the suite.

limitations: No Cubase execution or runtime differential comparison; this review concerns the local application wrapper.
No power-loss, filesystem replacement-failure, close-failure or concurrent external file-mutation fault injection. Publication ordering was reviewed; crash durability is not established.
Buffer-safety reasoning assumes valid AVAudioPCMBuffer backing storage. The public file path allocates its own buffers; arbitrary fabricated no-copy buffer descriptors are outside this reviewed use.
Core Audio readback establishes tested local format interoperability, not compatibility with every WAV reader. Source metadata and speaker labels are intentionally not preserved.
The six tests do not exercise near-4-GiB file writes; maximum-size arithmetic was checked statically and by bounded preflight tests.
C coefficient/state semantics and FP-domain restrictions are covered by the separately retained C review and candidate evidence, not rederived here.
